candidate.answerReason: The equal sides of ABC and the parallel construction imply BD = DE. Thus AD + DE = AB = 28, and the parallelogram has perimeter 56, matching choice C.

methods.label: Method 1: Equal base angles
methods.explanation:
A parallelogram's opposite sides are equal, so we only need the sum of two neighboring sides, \(AD+DE\). We can find this sum by showing that \(DE\) equals the remaining part \(DB\) of \(AB\).

Since \(AB=AC\), the base angles \(\angle ABC\) and \(\angle BCA\) are equal. In triangle \(BDE\), collinearity gives \(\angle DBE=\angle ABC\), and \(DE\parallel AC\) gives \(\angle BED=\angle BCA\). Thus \(\angle DBE=\angle BED\), so their opposite sides satisfy \(DE=BD\).

Consequently,
\[
AD+DE=AD+DB=AB=28.
\]
The perimeter of \(ADEF\) is therefore
\[
2(AD+DE)=2\cdot28=\boxed{56},
\]
choice \(\text{C}\).
methods.levelReason: Equal base angles, equal sides opposite equal angles, and parallelogram properties provide an elementary geometry solution.

methods.label: Method 2: Similar triangles
methods.explanation:
The parallel segment \(DE\) makes triangle \(BDE\) similar to triangle \(BAC\). Indeed, they have the same angle at \(B\), and \(DE\parallel AC\) gives \(\angle BDE=\angle BAC\), establishing similarity by two equal angles.

Corresponding sides therefore satisfy
\[
\frac{BD}{BA}=\frac{DE}{AC}.
\]
Because \(BA=AC=28\), this gives \(BD=DE\). Adding \(AD\) yields
\[
AD+DE=AD+DB=AB=28.
\]
Opposite sides of parallelogram \(ADEF\) are equal, so its perimeter is
\[
2(AD+DE)=2\cdot28=\boxed{56},
\]
choice \(\text{C}\).
methods.levelReason: AA similarity and corresponding-side ratios are standard school geometry within AMC 10 scope; no trigonometry is used.
